source_text: Sed iterum me dicis mihimetipsi esse contrarium, propositis videlicet aliis verbis meis, ubi propagationis officium a carnalis delectationis appetitione discernens: "Aliud esse dixi non concumbere nisi voluntate generandi, quod non habet culpam; aliud concumbendo carnis appetere voluptatem, sed non praeter coniugem, quod venialem habet culpam" … Calumniaris enim, "nos excusationem praebere turpibus et flagitiosis hominibus, ut cum infanda immunda commiserint, contra voluntatem se dicant fecisse, et ideo nullum habere peccatum"
pass_a_gloss: But again you say me to be contrary to my very self, having set forth namely other words of mine, where, distinguishing the duty of propagation from the seeking of carnal delight: 'One thing it is, I said, not to lie together except with the will of generating, which has no fault; another, in lying together to seek the pleasure of the flesh, but not beyond the spouse, which has venial fault'. For you slander 'that we furnish excuse to shameful and outrageous men, so that when they have committed unspeakable unclean things, they say they did (it) against will, and therefore have no sin'.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “But again you say that I contradict myself, setting out, of course, other words of mine, where, distinguishing the duty of propagation from the seeking of fleshly delight, I said: ‘It is one thing to lie together only with the will to beget, which has no fault; another, in lying together, to seek the pleasure of the flesh, but not outside one’s spouse, which has a pardonable fault.’”

“For you falsely charge ‘that we offer an excuse to shameful and wicked people, so that when they have committed unspeakable and unclean acts, they may say that they did it against their will, and therefore have no sin.’”

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
